title: Check that scripts produce correct json in render template action

timeline.message: Check that scripts produce correct json in render template action
timeline.author: Alan Woodward

timeline.body:
If a mustache script that outputs badly-formed json is referred to in a render
template request, then the error returned will be a 500 server error, rather than
a 400 json parsing error.  This is because rendering templates skips json parsing,
and so the error ends up being caught in the REST layer instead.

This commit changes the template rendering logic to always parse the output of
the script, catching json errors higher in the stack and allowing us to return 
the correct status code.  This also means that errors are correctly detected and
returned as part of multi search template requests.

Fixes #101477

This looks like a BWC break, but in fact this request would always throw an error via a REST request because the RestToXContentListener would try and parse things, but this test goes via the internal client which doesn't do any json parsing.

timeline.body:
This test appears to be passing, but for the wrong reason. The message from the exception thrown is:

```
org.elasticsearch.common.ParsingException: Unknown key for a START_OBJECT in [script].
```

Which reads like it's not even able to parse the script. Shouldn't the exception thrown here be `XContentParseException`?

reply.body: Oh, that's a good spot.  Interestingly, the test did fail without the fix, but it looks as though I'm not testing the specific scenario mentioned in the original issue.  I'll try and tidy up in a follow-up
